text:
Priya (Support): Hey team, urgent customer report — their function/tool call args are sometimes ending up as partial/malformed JSON when using streaming responses. Customer noticed missing trailing braces and invalid JSON during the stream, causing our function router to reject the call.

Sam (Customer): repro: calling /v1/generate with `stream=true` and `function_call` enabled. The model starts emitting `tool_call` with `args`, but last chunk cuts off mid-object: `{\"query\": \"get-items\", \"filters\": {\"date\": \"2025-01-01\", \"tags\": [\"prod\",` then stream ends. Parser fails.

Priya (Support): attaching customer trace and sample stream output below. They see it with both hosted and dedicated endpoints. No retries from client. They get a 400 from our function router: "invalid tool args: unexpected end of JSON input". Customer says it was intermittent over several calls.

Sam (Customer): pasted stream fragment: ```
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"search_db","args":"{\"query\": \"error rate\", \"limit\": 50, \"filters\": {\"env\": \"prod\", \"svc\": \"api\"}, \"cursor\": \"abc123\""

```
(note: last line has no closing quote/brace)

Lina (Support): I checked request IDs: `req-9b3f` and `req-9b40`. Both show streaming chunks ending with small partial payloads. No client disconnect reported.

Miguel (eng-runtime): looking. Two initial thoughts: 1) chunk boundary cutting because we treat `args` as string and then send chunks independently, so chunk size limit / prefix encoding could split inside a JSON string; 2) a framing/escape bug where we don't mark final chunk as `eof` for function_call events. Can you share raw chunk lengths?

Priya (Support): raw sizes from customer for req-9b3f: `[512, 512, 128]` and the last 128 ends mid-utf8 sequence according to their client. They reported same behavior with our SDK and curl.

Ava (eng-ml): Another angle: model can emit `args` as a stringified JSON; if we stream token-by-token and the consumer consumes lines, any line-based reassembly that expects `\n\n` delimiter can prematurely consider stream finished. Also if we apply truncation/quota at token level (billing), we might cut stream without app-level `done` event.

ops-sre: checking logs for transport resets. I see a handful of 499s in the same minute window for that POP but not correlated with all customer calls. No infra OOMs.

Miguel (eng-runtime): quick repro attempt on staging: calling model `gptx-mini` with `function_call=auto` and `stream=true`. I can reproduce partial args when enabling chunked transfer encoding and a low internal buffer_limit=600. Steps: ```
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"stream":true, "model":"gptx-mini", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"search for errors"}], "function_call":{"name":"search_db"}}' https://staging.redwood/api/generate | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Observed last chunk ended inside a JSON string.

Miguel (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: runtime's stream-slicer is splitting by bytes not logical tokens and doesn't guarantee chunk boundaries don't break JSON escapes. Also the function router expects well-formed JSON in `args` per-chunk reassembly; if last chunk lacks terminal closing brace and we do not emit an explicit `function_call_done` event, consumer attempts to parse prematurely.

Ava (eng-ml): plausible. We should ensure that when a function_call starts we either: a) stream `args` using structured framing (e.g., send each chunk as valid JSON substring with an explicit `more` flag), or b) buffer until we reach logical end before sending runnable function_call to router. Buffering trades latency for correctness.

Priya (Support): customer impact: their workflow treats `args` as JSON and auto-invokes downstream tools — they saw 15% failure rate across long queries. They're asking for mitigation asap (workaround or patch).

Miguel (eng-runtime): proposed short-term mitigation: detect when `args` appears to be started (leading `{`) and hold sending the `tool_call` event to the router until the streaming `data` sequence includes a closing `}` or we hit a safe max (e.g., 64k). Implement as a flag `defer_toolcall_until_complete`. This is quick and should reduce malformed-JSON errors.

Lina (Support): can we notify the customer with a workaround in the meantime? Suggest they disable streaming (stream=false) or have client-side reassembly that waits for final stream delimiter. Sam, would toggling to non-streaming be acceptable temporarily?

Sam (Customer): disabling streaming works for us but increases latency. Would prefer a server-side fix. Appreciate ETA.

Miguel (eng-runtime): I'll open a hotfix branch to add deferral behavior and add an explicit `event: function_call_end` marker when args complete. I suspect patch time ~ 2-3 dev hours + 1h QA. Will roll to staging first.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy of runtime/fix/stream-toolcall-deferral to staging at 2025-11-03T18:45Z · status: queued

Priya (Support): thanks — please post PR link and staging test id so I can coordinate with the customer. Also we need an alert rule to detect increased `invalid tool args` errors.

Miguel (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.redwood/repo/runtime/pull/542 (WIP). Staging test id: `stg-test-378`. Test steps included in PR.

Ava (eng-ml): additional test we should add: fuzzed tool args with embedded escaped braces and unicode to ensure chunk boundaries are safe for utf8. Also verify token/quota early cutoffs return a clear `stream_truncated` event.

ops-sre: I'll add a Grafana panel for `tool_router.invalid_args` and a 15-min alert if rate rises by 3x baseline.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2025-4113, severity: P3, owner: Miguel (eng-runtime) — link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-4113

Lina (Support): I'll update the customer: suggest temporary `stream=false` and notify once staging deploy passes.

Sam (Customer): thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.

Miguel (eng-runtime): follow-up notes: patch adds `function_call_fragment` framing with `is_final` boolean sent as metadata for each fragment; router will only attempt JSON parse when `is_final=true` or on aggregate. This avoids buffering whole payloads on all calls. Will instrument metrics `toolcall.fragmented` and `toolcall.early_parse_error`.

Priya (Support): perfect. keep me posted on staging deploy result. :thumbsup:
